newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Return on Brazil B Band investment seen at 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Return on Brazil B Band investment seen at 15 pct.

text.p: Brazil's federally owned Banco do Brasil said it foresees a minimum 15 percent annual return on its investment in B Band cellular services.

"In the opinion of the investment bank of Banco do Brasil, the real return on investment from the development of private cellular services will reach at least 15 percent a year," the bank said in a statement.

The bank's BB Investimentos and Previ pension fund are partners in Americel, a consortium that last week won a license to operate in B Band frequency area seven in central and western Brazil, including the capital of Brasilia.
The group -- led by Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc, and Telesystem, also Canadian; and including local Opportunity bank and Citibank -- is also bidding for licenses in six other B Band areas.
As the Telet consortium, the partners are hoping to win prized concessions covering Sao Paulo city and state, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais.
"The winning firms will invest, in the next five years between $12 billion and $15 billion, in both licenses and operating investments," the statement said.
